technologies.name: Parchment
technologies.description: Unlocks parchment and allows you to create written material.
technologies.flavor: Parchment became an important carrier of information in the ancient world.

technologies.name: Mathematics
technologies.description: -10% to the work cost of construction.
technologies.flavor: Ancient civilizations could count, but only now has knowledge moved from simple recipes to strict proofs. Geometry and abstract calculation let people not just watch the world but compute it: from the shape of a wheel's teeth to the motion of the stars.

technologies.name: Calendar
technologies.description: +30% to resource production on plantations.
technologies.flavor: People have tracked the turning of the seasons since the earliest times, but only now has the calendar become a standard tool of management: precise planning of sowing, pruning and harvest let plantations reach their full potential.

technologies.name: Road Paving
technologies.description: Unlocks Paved Roads (road level 3): up to 50 units/sec per section.
technologies.flavor: A firm bed of rubble carries the weight; fitted stones hold the surface together. When the rains come, loaded carts can still reach the city.

technologies.name: Draft Animals
technologies.description: Unlocks the use of draft animals to turn millstones.
technologies.flavor: Draft animals let people harness animal strength for heavy work, greatly raising output and efficiency in farming and construction.

technologies.name: Water Wheel
technologies.description: Unlocks the water mill: the running water sets the millstones in motion.
technologies.flavor: The water wheel became an important source of power in the ancient world, automating the processing of grain and other materials.

technologies.name: Cog Wheel
technologies.description:
Unlocks the toothed wheel: the gears that pass a rotation on to the working tool.
+25% to the production of mines, quarries, animal mills, oil mills, oilmaker's, weaver's and silkmaker's houses and weaver's, mason's, carpenter's and jeweler's workshops.
technologies.flavor: A wheel that rolls is not yet a machine; the teeth are. They turn one turn of the axle into a turn of the millstone, a pull of the press or a lift of the winch, and they hold the load instead of letting it fall back. Vitruvius described a mill whose upright wheel drove a horizontal one through a row of teeth, and a marble saw driven the same way is known from a sarcophagus in Hierapolis.

technologies.name: Screw Press
technologies.description: Adds one production slot to the winemaker's house, the oilmaker's house, the dairy, the paper workshop and the jeweler's house.
technologies.flavor: A threaded spindle turns many easy turns of a long handle into one slow, enormous squeeze. The press no longer waits on the weight of a beam, and a second batch can be worked beside the first.

technologies.name: Hoisting Mechanisms
technologies.description: +10% to the production of mines and quarries.
technologies.flavor: A shaft is only as deep as the rope that serves it. A drum on a windlass, a rope over a pulley, a capstan walked round by men or oxen — and in the Chinese mines a treadwheel the size of a house, turning all day like the water wheel it resembles. What the hoist brings up is what the mine is worth: the ore that cannot be lifted stays in the rock.

technologies.name: Mechanics
technologies.description:
Adds one production slot to the animal mill and the water mill.
+10% to the production of the woodcutter's camp.
technologies.flavor: The workshops knew the lever and the pulley long before anyone wrote them down. Heron of Alexandria set the pieces in order in his Mechanics, and later al-Khazini weighed the same pieces of rope and iron in the Book of the Balance of Wisdom. A machine, they wrote, is what moves a load we could not lift: a wheel on an axle, a crank, a connecting rod, a frame to hold it all. From this the hoist, the press and the mill stop being clever tricks and become craft — they can be built again, and then improved.

technologies.name: Water Power
technologies.description: Enables water-powered upgrades for the paper workshop and forge. +25% production for mines, quarries, bloomeries and smelters only where fresh water is available.
technologies.flavor: Turning a millstone was only the first errand given to a river. Once cams and levers were fitted to the axle of the wheel, steady rotation became a measured stroke: Han ironmasters led streams to push the bellows of their furnaces day and night, ore stamps pounded vein-rock beside mountain sluices, and heavy trip hammers beat glowing blooms on the anvil without tiring.

technologies.name: Precision Instruments
technologies.description: Unlocks precision instruments crafted from copper, bronze, brass, iron or steel in the forge and the jeweler's house.
technologies.flavor: Between the smith's hammer and the scholar's theorem lies a quiet threshold: the moment a hand learns to divide a circle evenly, balance a beam to a grain and file a pivot that does not wobble. Once geometry, gearing and clean metalwork met at one bench — in Han bronze calipers and armillary rings, in Hellenistic dioptras and geared spheres, in the assay balances of al-Khazini and the astrolabe-makers' workshops — any sound metal could be turned into an instrument that measured rather than guessed.

technologies.name: Paper
technologies.description:
Allows you to build the paper workshop.
Allows you to produce paper from mulberry, hemp and ramie with the help of lime.
technologies.flavor: This revolutionary invention made it possible to create an affordable, practical material for writing.

technologies.name: Scriptoriums
technologies.description: Allows you to build scriptoriums.
technologies.flavor: In scriptoriums scribes copied, translated, rewrote and recensioned texts on administration, the worship of the gods, magic and the curing of disease.

technologies.name: Bookbinding
technologies.description:
Allows you to build the bookbinder's workshop.
Allows you to bind sheets of parchment or paper into books with leather and glue.
technologies.flavor: The codex did not need to be unrolled: it opened at any page the reader chose and held the whole work between two covers. Sewing the sheets through the fold and gluing a tanned hide into a cover turned a sheaf of writing into a thing that could be shelved, carried and sold.

technologies.name: Cartography
technologies.description: Allows scouts to explore areas in the fog of war.
technologies.flavor: The art of exploring the land and drawing maps of it.

unlock_effects.name: Allows scouts to explore areas in the fog of war.

technologies.name: Emporia
technologies.description: Allows you to build improvements on explored resource hexes outside the Region. Such an outpost needs a road to the city and costs coins on top of labour; the further from the city, the more expensive.
technologies.flavor: An emporion was neither a colony nor a city: a foothold on a foreign shore where the road met the sea and goods changed hands.

unlock_effects.name: Allows you to build improvements on explored resource hexes outside the Region.

technologies.name: Alchemy
technologies.description: Allows you to build the alchemist's house, opens saltpeter, borax and sal ammoniac deposits, and unlocks green vitriol, iron-gall ink and ceramic glaze.
technologies.flavor: A protoscience of attempts to turn base metals into gold.

technologies.name: Steel Making
technologies.description: Unlocks steel in the forge and the goods forged of it.
technologies.flavor: Iron with a little carbon is another metal. Charcoal driven into a hot bloom and a flux that keeps the melt clean give a smith an edge that holds and a blade that does not bend.

technologies.name: Glassblowing
technologies.description: Unlocks recipe for glass bottles.
technologies.flavor: The first step towards the modern glass industry.

technologies.name: Concrete
technologies.description: Reveals the mountain springs and allows you to build aqueducts: a channel of concrete brings fresh water from a spring to the city.
technologies.flavor: Lime burned in a kiln, mixed with sand and stone, sets into a mass harder than the rock it came from. A channel lined with it keeps its slope and its walls for generations, so water can leave the mountain and reach a city that has no river of its own.

unlock_effects.name: Reveals mountain springs and allows you to build aqueducts to the city.

technologies.name: Shipbuilding
technologies.description:
Allows you to build the sailmaker's workshop and the boatyard.
Unlocks fast sailcloth production and wooden boats rigged with cloth sails.
technologies.flavor: A bundle of reeds floats only until it swells with water; a planked hull keeps the water outside. Sawn boards joined edge to edge over curved ribs, stayed with twisted cordage and driven by a square of heavy canvas let boatmen leave the shallows behind, work deeper fishing grounds in rough weather and carry timber and grain along every river and coast.

technologies.name: Coinage
technologies.description:
Allows you to build the Mint, which strikes coins for the city.
Each batch of coin leaves a seigniorage in the treasury: the more metal a strike takes, the more coin the treasury keeps.
technologies.flavor: A weighed piece of metal bearing a ruler's mark turned a bargain into a debt that could be counted. Stamped ingots appeared in Lydia and in the Zhou lands; the stamp made the coin a promise the next town would accept.

unlock_effects.name: Mint: coins struck from copper, silver or gold pay a seigniorage

technologies.name: Assaying
technologies.description:
The master of the Mint now tests the metal as well as strikes it: +50% to the seigniorage of the coins.
Consumes precision instruments.
technologies.flavor: Weighing is only the first answer. Before the die falls, the metal must be cupelled with lead, parted and read for fineness. In the assay houses of Serica, in the Hellenistic mints and in the workshops where al-Khazini set his balances true, this craft taught men to promise a coin a stranger could trust. The Mint takes the assayer's bench into its own hall.

technologies.name: Navigation
technologies.description:
Allows outposts on scouted coastal and island resource hexes without a road to the city. The water beside the hex must have a harbour.
Sea outposts deliver their produce straight to the city.
technologies.flavor: A road stops at the shore; a hull does not. The pilot reads the swell, the stars and the flight of shorebirds, and the island that no highway can reach takes its place in the same ledger as the inland farm. The monsoon sailors of the Indian Ocean, the island navigators of the Pacific and the coastwise skippers of the northern seas kept no single school: each taught the harbour master the same lesson — the sea is a road that needs no paving.

unlock_effects.name: Allows outposts on coasts and islands without a road

technologies.name: Astronomy
technologies.description: Orientation by the stars lets scholars work 15% faster.
technologies.flavor: The ploughman reads the seasons and the sailor reads the swell, but the traveller beyond both needs a sky that does not change. Star paths were measured in the camps of the steppe, on the reefs of the Pacific, in the caravans of the desert and in the observatories of Serica and Alexandria; the same fixed points led a caravan across the sand and a hull across dark water. With the astrolabe at his belt the scholar could teach the angle of a star to an apprentice and give the distant road a name.

technologies.name: Foreign Trade
technologies.description: The knowledge that opens the way to markets beyond the known world.
technologies.flavor: A market at the edge of the known world is not the end of trade. Merchants who knew the stars and the carry of a hull sent their wares past the last road, to ports and courts no map of the region showed: the bargain was written in the ledger of the city, not on its fields. The caravanserai of the steppe and the counting houses of the monsoon coast kept the same book.
